title: Najahid Dynasty
capsule: The Najahids were a dynasty of Abyssinian (Ethiopian) Mamluk origin who ruled the Tihama coastal plain of Yemen from their capital at Zabid, founded after Najah, a former slave of the Ziyadid rulers, established independent authority around 1022. The dynasty's rule was interrupted by the Sulaymanid dynasty but reasserted, and the Najahids maintained control of the lucrative Red Sea trade routes and the agriculturally productive Tihama lowlands for over a century. Their rule ended in 1158 when the Mahdid dynasty displaced them at Zabid; the region subsequently passed to Ayyubid control under Turan-Shah in 1174.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Najahids are attested in Arabic chronicles but their territorial extent is poorly mapped; control over the Tihama lowlands is established while precise northern and eastern boundaries are uncertain.
